SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_ALWAYSUSECRIT_HINT: Check to enable critical success and failure on non-combat rolls - automatically enabled if crits are selected
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_MORERITUALS_HINT: Check to enable more rituals as described on Advanced Players Guide p. 103
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_AUTOCOMBAT_HINT: Check to enable QoL enhancement for smooth combat. Read the Symbaroum system guide for FoundryVTT in the compendium section for more info
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_SAVECOMBATROLL_HINT: Check to enable QoL enhancement for keeping all modifiers when rolling combat (weapon/defense)
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_SAVEATTRIBUTEROLL_HIN: Check to enable QoL enhancement for keeping all modifiers when rolling attribute tests
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_SHOWMODIFIERSINDIALOG: Show modifers in targetted attribute rolls
Check to enable QoL enhancement for showing attribute modifiers before making the roll
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_NPC_MODIFIERS_HINT: Check to show NPC modifiers (-5 to +5) instead of attributes for NPCs on character sheet
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_INIATITIVEROLLS_HINT: Check to QoL disabling of Initiative rolls in chat
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_AUTOROLLINITIATIVE: Automatically roll initiative at start of combat
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_AUTOROLLINITIATIVE_HI: Check to enable automatic initiative at start of combat
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_SHOWREFERENCE_HINT: Warning - GM Only - allow to manually adjust reference implementation for abilities, traits and mystical powers. Requires refresh.
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_INIT_MANUAL_HINT: Check to de-active the automated evaluation of the attribute used for initiative.
SYMBAROUM.SETTING_CURRENCY_SHILLING_ORTE: How many Orteg one Shilling is worth. Default 10 (1 Thaler = 10 Shilling = 100 Orteg).
SYMBAROUM.SETTING_CURRENCY_THALER_SHILLI: How many Shilling one Thaler is worth. Default 10 (1 Thaler = 10 Shilling = 100 Orteg).
SYMBAROUM.SETTING_ENCUMBRANCE_ENABLED_HI: Enables the optional encumbrance rules from the Advanced Player's Guide: weight category on item sheets, an encumbrance bar in the Attributes tab and a Defense penalty above the load limit (Strength). Default: off.
SYMBAROUM.SETTING_ENCUMBRANCE_HARD_LIMIT: The hard encumbrance limit is Strength × this factor (APG default 2). Beyond it, a character can only move short distances.
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_RESET_NOTE: NOTE: Submit and Reset will cause FVTT to reload.
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_CONFIG_MENUHINT: Configure PC and NPC sheet background color (These are Client based settings).
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_ADD_MENUHINT: Add Colour setting button to Main Config panel.
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_PLAYER_RESIST_HINT: When NPCs use powers that can be resisted, or attack with Combat Enhancement options, instead of rolling directly this option creates a button in the relevant player Chat that the Player will have to click on for the resist roll to be done.
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_NPC_ATTACKS: Show multiple attacks in the weapon box for NPCs
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_NPC_ATTACKS_HINT: Warning: the system tries it best to process this, but can't integrate some traits / abilities that are situationnal or complex.
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_ENHANCEDDEATHSAVEBONU: Death save bonus applies for crit
Any death save bonus applies to the odds of critical success, i.e. either improve or remove chance of critical success of death saves
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_ALLROLLSDICESONICE: Dice so Nice module on all rolls
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_ALLROLLSDICESONICE_HI: When the Dice so Nice module is added and Enhanced Combat option is enabled, a lot of dice can be thrown at the same time on the screen. By default, only the base d20 action roll will be displayed. Check this option if you prefer to have all dice displayed (damage, poison, etc).
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_SHOWLOCALLANGPACK_HIN: Will only show language compendium that matches your chosen language and the english macro & system compendium
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_SHOWENGLISHPACKS: Include all english compendium with the chosen language
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_SHOWENGLISHPACKS_HINT: In addition to your chosen language, it will also show all english compendiums
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_HIDEENGLISHMACROS: Exclude English macro and system compendium
SYMBAROUM.OPTIONAL_HIDEENGLISHMACROS_HIN: Exclude the English system and macro compendiums, which are shown otherwise
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CONFIG_SETTINGS_CONTENT: To get to the Symbaroum configuration, click the 'Game Settings' icon
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CONFIG_CONFIGURE_CONTENT: Select the 'Configure Settings' for the settings for Foundry, Symbaroum and all modules
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CONFIG_SYSSETTINGS_CONTEN: To see the Symbaroum specific settings, select Symbaroum in the panel
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CONFIG_SYMBSETTINGS_CONTE: The 'Configure Symbaroum settings' allows tailoring of colours and background images used in the system
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CONFIG_SYMBSETTINGS_GS_CO: The 'Configure Symbaroum settings' is also available directly under the 'Game Settings'
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CONFIG_SYMBSETTINGS_EC_CO: Enhanced combat, nicknamed EC, can be turned on here for combat automation
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CONFIG_SYMBSETTINGS_ALL_C: There are quite a few settings for Symbaroum that might have a better fit at your table
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CONFIG_SYSGUIDE_JOURNALS_: For further information and details, go to 'Journals'
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CONFIG_SYSGUIDE_DOC_CONTE: The Symbaroum System guide comes automatically with the system and is recommended reading
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_COMPENDIUMS: As default a new world starts empty
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_COMPENDIUMS_CONTENT: However, with Free Leagues permission, we can help you fill it
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_ADVENTURECOMPENDIUM_CONTE: The Symbaroum adventure compendium contains all that you need to get started
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_ADVENTURECOMPENDIUM_HIGHL: Clicking on an adventure will allow you to import content into your world
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_ACTOR_ERROR: For a player to complete this, the GM needs to run through the GM tour and not delete 'Beremo' in the actor catalogue
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CHARACTER_ACTORTAB_CONTEN: Under the actor tab, you find all actors (players/npc) that you or module have created for you
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CHARACTER_ACTORTAB_CREATE: The create actor button will prompt for name (mandatory) and type (player/npc). Lets create an actor for you.
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CHARACTER_SELECTACTOR_CON: We created the character Beremo for you. When its name is clicked, it will open up the character sheet
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CHARACTER_HEADER_CONTENT: The header contains information such as name, xp (see more in system guide), race and more
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CHARACTER_TABS_CONTENT: These are the different sections for the character sheet - we will come back to these
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CHARACTER_ATTRIBUTES_CONT: This is the list of attributes for this character
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CHARACTER_ATTRIBUTES_ACCU: This is the value of characters accurate, note the field is read-only (indicated by the blue-ish background)
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CHARACTER_ATTRIBUTES_CONF: To change attribute values, click on this cog-wheel. Normally you just change the Base value. The mod value is reserved for alternate damage
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CHARACTER_COMBAT_ARMOR_CO:
This is the quick link for active armor. Clicking on the this will roll defense.
Note that when using enhanced combat then this button does not do anything
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CHARACTER_COMBAT_WEAPON_C: This is the quick link for active weapon(s).  Clicking on these will try to use the weapon in combat.
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CHARACTER_COMBAT_ABILITIE: This contains the list of abilities, traits, powers, rituals, boons and burdens the character have. The exp for these are automatically totalled in the exp field
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CHARACTER_GEAR_CONTENT: The GEAR tab is where you can make modifications to your equipment, such as wear it or rename it
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CHARACTER_GEAR_ARMOR_CONT: This is the armor owned by the character, be it active, equipped or just owned
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CHARACTER_GEAR_ARMOR_EQUI: Gear have three states, active (being used), equipped (being worn) or other (stashed/owned but not here). Only Active gear appear on the first tab (MAIN)
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CHARACTER_GEAR_ARMOR_NAME: This is the name of the armor, clicking on this will open the armors configuration screen for this character
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CHARACTER_BIO_CONTENT: This contains the bio of the character.
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CHARACTER_BIO_SHADOW_CONT: For example, here is the characters shadow
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CHARACTER_NOTES_CONTENT: This tab is here so that the character can keep notes and other information
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CHARACTER_NOTES_FIELD_CON:
This is where the character can write details - to activate click on the top right icon that appears when moving the mouse here.
This wraps up this tour, we will leave the character so that players can run through this tour
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_CHARACTER_OVERVIEW_CONTEN: Good luck, and please check the System guide for more information
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_ACOMPENDIUM_GOTOCONTENT: You will find the Symbaroum system adventure compendium under the compendium tab
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_ACOMPENDIUM_SYSTEM_CONTEN: The Symbaroum system compendium can be opened here
SYMBAROUM.TOUR_ACOMPENDIUM_SYSTEM_ENGLIS: There are many compendiums here with translated content. If you import them, pick the one for your language
This is the English compendium and information about it
This is items that this compendium contains and will move into your world
You click here to start the import - be patient and allow it to complete before running another one
MODERN.SHADOW_HINT: Shadow: visible to the GM and the character owner only
MODERN.MONEY_HINT: Click to edit – thaler/shilling/orteg with delta syntax (e.g. +3 or -2)
MODERN_ITEM.PRICE_HINT: Click to edit – price (orteg base value) with delta syntax (e.g. +3 or -2)
MODERN.FAVORITES_EMPTY: No favorites yet – click the star on an item (per character).
MODERN.EXP_HINT: Only total XP and reroll points are editable; the points spent on abilities derive from the learned items.
MODERN.GAUGE_NOTE: white marker = load limit · only with the optional rule active
MODERN.MOVE_DENIED: Not allowed: you own neither the source nor the target actor.
MODERN.DESIGN_TITLE: Design Settings – Alternative Player and Monster Sheets
SYMBAROUM.SETTING_MODERNSHEET_ENABLED_HI: Enables the modernized sheet view (sidebar, icon tabs for combat, abilities & powers, gear, biography and notes). Every user can toggle between the classic and modernized view from the sheet header. Default: off (classic view).
SYMBAROUM.SETTING_MODERNSHEET_DESIGN_HIN: Color scheme, load gauge variant, tab icons and default view of the alternative sheets (GM only).
SYMBAROUM.SETTING_MODERNSHEET_DESIGN_TIT: Design Settings – Alternative Player and Monster Sheets
CONTAINER.CAPACITY_TOOLTIP: Container capacity in weight units. 0 = unlimited. Display only in v1 – drops are not blocked.
CONTAINER.PACKED: Packed – state "Other" (does not fight, not counted individually)
CONTAINER.WEIGHTLESS_HINT: Bag of holding: contents do not count toward load.
CONTAINER.MONEY_TOOLTIP: Money in the container (including nested containers)
CONTAINER.MONEY_TRANSFER_HINT: Positive amount = deposit from the actor into the container, negative = withdraw from the container. 0 = no change.
CONTAINER.RECIPES_VALUE: Recipe value in the container (sum of contained recipes)
CONTAINER.CURRENCY_SHEET_HINT: Money in the container in Orteg (base value). Player flow: right-click the container row in the gear tab.
CONTAINER.DELETE_HINT: Delete: the contents can be returned to the inventory or deleted as well.
CONTAINER.DELETE_RETURN_CONFIRM: Delete "{name}"? {count} contained item(s) will be returned to the inventory.
CONTAINER.DELETE_PURGE_CONFIRM: Irreversibly delete "{name}" and its {count} contained item(s)?
CONTAINER.WARN_NOT_GEAR: Only weapons, armors, equipment, artifacts and containers can be stored.
CONTAINER.WARN_SELF: A container cannot contain itself (or a container that contains it).
CONTAINER.WARN_MAX_DEPTH: Containers cannot be nested more than {depth} levels deep.
CONTAINER.WARN_NO_ACTOR_MONEY: The actor does not have that much money.
CONTAINER.WARN_NO_CONTAINER_MONEY: There is not that much money in the container.
MACRO.CONTAINER_MIGRATION_HEADER: Equipment found with container names (backpack, pouch, chest …). On accept, each item is converted to the "container" type – name, image, description, weight and price carry over.
MACRO.CONTAINER_MIGRATION_HINT: Capacity 0 = unlimited. No RAW values are suggested – please review per container before accepting.
MACRO.CONTAINER_MIGRATION_NONE: No equipment with container names found.
MODERN_ITEM.REFERENCE_TOOLTIP: Technical RAW key (e.g. „regeneration”) by which automations (hooks, combat values, enricher) recognize this item. Set by the GM on custom/compendium imports; on weapons: weapon class.
GIVE.QUANTITY_TOOLTIP: 1 up to the number in stock
GIVE.CONTAINER_NOTE: The container is transferred in full, including its contents.
GIVE.TARGET_OFFLINE: The recipient is not online – hand-over cancelled.
GIVE.NO_RIGHTS: You lack the permissions for this hand-over.
GIVE.RATIONS_QUANTITY_TOOLTIP: 1 up to the available ration stock
LOOT.SETTING_ENABLED_ON_DEATH_HINT: NPC tokens (actor type monster) automatically become lootable when their toughness drops to 0. Overridable per token/actor via the loot settings on the token (HUD gear icon). Only processed by the active GM.
LOOT.SETTING_DELETE_EMPTY_HINT: Loot piles created via canvas drag disappear once their last item and their money have been taken. Defeated NPC tokens always remain. Overridable per pile via the loot settings on the token.
LOOT.CONFIG_ENABLED: Loot enabled (players loot with a single click)
LOOT.CONFIG_DELETE_HINT: Applies only to loot piles from canvas drag — {name} remains as a defeated NPC.
LOOT.ACTOR_HINT: Death automation only applies to NPC (monster) actors.
LOOT.ACTOR_APPLY: These settings apply as defaults for this actor's tokens unless a token defines its own.
LOOT.DROP_HINT: The item is placed as a loot pile at this location and removed from its source (if it belongs to an actor).
LOOT.ERR_NO_GM: No GM online — loot action unavailable.
LOOT.ERR_EMPTY: There is nothing to loot here.
RESOURCE_CATEGORY.LABEL: Resource category
RESOURCE_CATEGORY.TOOLTIP: Assigns this item to a consumable resource category. Herbal cure: the medicus roll deducts 1 upon rolling (setting "Resource consumption"). Alchemy ingredient: abstract brewing materials, 1 unit = 1 shilling of material value; consumed via the "Consume resource" context menu until the brewing dialog exists.
RESOURCE.SETTING_ENABLED_HINT: Category-based consumption automation: the medicus roll deducts 1 herbal cure upon rolling (regardless of the result) and the cure heals 1 toughness point even on a failed roll - except on a critical fumble. If no herbal cure is in the inventory, the check box in the roll dialog is greyed out. The "Consume resource" context menu remains available regardless of this setting.
RESOURCE.ERR_NONE_LEFT: Not enough of the resource in the inventory.
RESOURCE.ERR_NONE_LEFT_MEDICUS: No herbal cure (resource category) left in the inventory - the roll proceeds without herbal cure.
AMMO.SETTING_ENABLED_HINT: Weapon-side ammunition automation: weapons with an ammunition category set (GM field on the weapon sheet) deduct amount × number of attacks from the ammunition stacks (resource category) on roll submit – regardless of the roll result. If not enough ammunition is available, the attack is refused (notification, no roll). Thrown weapons (thrown weapon class + stackable) consume themselves: −1 per attack. Mid-chain attacks (returning swing, double strike) book nothing.
AMMO.SETTING_RECOVERY_HINT: Unlocks the recovery macro (recovering ammunition after combat): one d20 per spent projectile, recovered on a roll ≤ threshold (standard 10, quality 15, mystical quality 17). The recovery macro is delivered separately and is used by players (own character) and the GM (actor choice). Only takes effect if “Ammunition consumption” is active as well.
AMMO.CATEGORY_TOOLTIP: Ammunition category of this weapon (GM): empty = no consumption. If the "Ammunition consumption" setting is active, roll submit deducts amount × number of attacks from the stacks of this resource category; without sufficient stock the attack is refused.
AMMO.AMOUNT_TOOLTIP: Amount deducted from the ammunition stacks per attack (default 1, minimum 1).
AMMO.ERR_NO_AMMO: No ammunition ({category}) in inventory – attack with {weapon} refused.
AMMO.ERR_NOT_ENOUGH: Not enough ammunition ({category}) for {attacks} attacks with {weapon} – roll refused.
AMMO.ERR_NO_THROWN: No {weapon} left in the stack – attack refused.
AMMO.ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_THROWN: Not enough {weapon} in the stack for {attacks} attacks – roll refused.
AMMO.ERR_NO_SPECIAL_AMMO: Not enough special ammunition ({amount} needed) – roll refused.
ALCHEMY_LEVEL.LABEL: Alchemy Level
ALCHEMY_LEVEL.TOOLTIP: Elixir level – drives level-dependent values (fog orb penalty, flash dust rounds, dice steps).
AMMO_EFFECT.LABEL: Ammunition Effect
AMMO_EFFECT.TOOLTIP: Alchemical ammunition: the stun bolt fires the Strong–[damage] test automatically on a hit, the homing arrow adds a hint line to the attack card.
COMBAT.CHAT_SEEKINGARROW_HINT: Homing arrow ({ammo}): needs no clear line of sight, but the archer must see part of the target – normal attack roll.
EPILEPSY.AUTOPARAM: Epileptic fit (−{penalty} on all success rolls)
EPILEPSY.CARD_LINE: {name} rolls a natural 20: the burden Epileptic triggers a fit.
EPILEPSY.CARD_EXHAUSTION: Exhausted afterwards: −1 on all success rolls until the end of the scene.
ELIXIR.ALCHEMICAL_TOOLTIP: Marks this item as alchemical: only then do the alchemy entries (level, usage, ammunition effect, effect fields) and the “Use elixir” menu entry appear. Preselected as “Yes” when effect fields are already filled.
ELIXIR.USAGE_TOOLTIP: Controls what “Use elixir” does on this item: automatic self-application, throw dialog with target test, narrative card, or ammunition hint.
ELIXIR.EFFECT_HINT: GM fields of the elixir automation – numbers or dice formulas (1d6); “Causes condition”, “Resist test” and “Attribute modification” are selection lists, attribute values are read from the bonus tab. The elixir tagging macro sets the defaults.
ELIXIR.FIELD_HEAL_TOOLTIP: Number – immediate toughness healing (holy water: 2, herbal cure: 1).
ELIXIR.FIELD_HEAL_PER_ROUND_TOOLTIP: Number or dice formula – healing per active round via the round engine (elixir of life: 1d6).
ELIXIR.FIELD_ROUNDS_TOOLTIP: Duration of per-round effects/conditions: number or dice formula (elixir of life: 1d6). 0 = one-shot, takes effect immediately.
ELIXIR.FIELD_CORRUPTION_REMOVE_TOOLTIP: Number or dice formula – immediately removes that much temporary corruption (purple sap: 1d4/1d6/1d8).
ELIXIR.FIELD_CORRUPTION_GAIN_TOOLTIP: Number – adds that much temporary corruption.
ELIXIR.FIELD_CORRUPTION_PER_ROUND_TOOLTI: Number or dice formula – temporary corruption per active round (elixir of life: 1).
ELIXIR.FIELD_CONDITION_TOOLTIP: Yes/No selection – with “Yes” the gear button opens the condition dialog (multi-select); the chosen conditions are applied with the round duration on use. With “No” chosen conditions stay stored but never apply.
ELIXIR.CONDITION_DIALOG_INTRO: Tick one or more conditions – they apply with the duration on use (multi-select).
ELIXIR.FIELD_ATTRMODE_TOOLTIP: Selection instead of legacy free text: “Yes – fixed values” applies all filled attribute fields from the bonus tab (wild chew), “Yes – choice” lets the user pick ONE filled value when applying (war paint, dialog in the throw path). Values are maintained in the item's bonus tab.
ELIXIR.FIELD_ATTRMODS_TOOLTIP: Comma list “attr±N”, “|” marks a choice (war paint: quick+1|strong+1; wild chew: quick+2,strong+2,accurate+2,discreet-2,cunning-2,resolute-2).
ELIXIR.FIELD_DAMAGE_TOOLTIP: Dice formula – immediate damage on a thrown hit (boom stone: 1d4/1d6/1d8).
ELIXIR.FIELD_DAMAGE_PER_ROUND_TOOLTIP: Dice formula – damage per round via the acid engine (acid sphere: 1d4/1d6/1d8).
ELIXIR.FIELD_RESIST_TOOLTIP: Attribute selection – one-sided resist test on a thrown hit (flash dust: quick, fog orb: strong). “None” = the condition applies unimpeded.
ELIXIR.FIELD_TARGET_CONDITION_TOOLTIP: Condition id on a failed target test (flash dust: blind, fog orb: dazed).
ELIXIR.FIELD_TARGET_CONDITION_ROUNDS_TOO: Number or dice formula (flash dust: 1d6/1d4/1, fog orb: 1d4).
ELIXIR.REMOVE_CONDITION_TOOLTIP: Condition the application heals on the user (eye drops: blind) – applied via the GM application card.
ELIXIR.FIELD_NOTE_TOOLTIP: Free text – shown as an effect line on the chat card (antidote, ghost dust, candles, coatings …).
ELIXIR.ERR_NO_ACTOR: This elixir belongs to no character – only inventoried elixirs can be used.
ELIXIR.ERR_NO_USAGE: {name} is not tagged as an elixir (no usage set).
ELIXIR.ERR_NO_TARGETS: No target tokens on this scene.
ELIXIR.ERR_BAD_ATTRMODS: Invalid attribute shift: “{value}” (syntax: attr+N / attr-N, choice with |).
ELIXIR.AMMO_HINT: {name} takes effect on the next weapon attack – the stack is deducted automatically (world setting “Ammunition consumption”).
ELIXIR.CHAT_NO_EFFECT_FIELDS: No machine-readable effect fields tagged – the rules effect remains with the GM.
ELIXIR.CHAT_DAMAGE_PER_ROUND: {target} suffers {formula} damage per round for {rounds} rounds (acid).
ELIXIR.CHAT_ATTR_SYMBOL: Bonus symbol applied – deleting the symbol automatically reverts the bonuses.
ELIXIR.CHAT_ATTR_REVERTED: {name}: elixir bonuses removed – attribute shifts reverted.
ELIXIR.CHAT_SL_NOTE: {name} unfolds its effect – the GM applies the rules effect.
ELIXIR.CHAT_ANTIDOT: Antidote grade {grade}: reduces the poison's round damage by {amount} points.
ELIXIR.FIELD_ANTIDOT_TOOLTIP: Marks the elixir as an antidote of grade 1–3: applying it to a poisoned target reduces the constant round damage by 2 points per grade; at 0 or below the poison is cured (status icon disappears). Not for proactive use.
POISON.ERR_NO_DOSE_BY_GRADE: No poison dose of grade {grade} left in inventory.
DIALOG.POISON_COATING_HINT: Coats the weapon with 1 dose of the selected weapon poison. The coating stays in effect until a poisoning succeeds (the dose is only booked then; hits in later rounds carry the poison as well). "No poison" permanently wipes the persistent AND the active scene coating – a new dose must be applied. On a hit: target's Strength–[damage] resist test; on failure a poison DoT (round damage rolled once and constant, rolled duration).
DIALOG.POISON_MASTER_FAVOUR_PARAM: Master Poisoner: favour on the poison test
DIALOG.POISON_MANUAL_HINT: Fixed +1 bonus on the poisoner's poison test and the weapon coating test – not on the attack roll.
COMBAT.CHAT_POISON_COATING_SUCCESS: is poisoned. Damage per round: {damage}, duration {rounds} rounds.
COMBAT.CHAT_POISON_RESILIENT_NEUTRALIZED: is fully neutralized by Poison Resilient – no poison damage.
MACRO.BERGEN_GATE_OFF: Recovery disabled – the world settings “Ammo consumption” and “Ammo recovery” must be enabled.
MACRO.BERGEN_NO_CANDIDATES_OWN: No actor with recoverable projectiles among your characters.
MACRO.BERGEN_NO_CANDIDATES_WORLD: No actor with recoverable projectiles in this world.
MACRO.BERGEN_STACK_QUESTION: Which ammunition stack do you recover from?
ELIXIR.FIELD_WEAPON_POISON_TOOLTIP: Marks the elixir as a weapon poison: the roll dialog offers “Apply poison” (1 dose is consumed). Poison DoT from “Damage/round” (falling back to “Damage”), duration rolled from “Rounds”; the round damage is rolled once on application and stays constant.
ELIXIR.CHAT_NO_COMBAT_FULL: No active combat — full effect applied immediately.
POISON.ANTIDOT_REDUCED: {name}: poison mitigated — round damage reduced to {damage}, {rounds} rounds remaining.
BREW.SETTING_ECONOMY_HINT: Economy mode of the brew dialog: elixirs require owned recipes (ownership owned/bound) and consume alchemy ingredients — half the elixir's list price in shillings per dose; success books per dose, failure books the raw material of the attempt. Off (RAW): all tagged world elixirs brewable, no ingredient booking.
BREW.FROM_RECIPE_TOOLTIP: Open the brewing dialog with this recipe
BREW.BUTTON_TOOLTIP: Brew elixir — open the brew dialog (Cunning test with lab bonus)
BREW.LAB_TOOLTIP: Laboratory in the inventory — bonus on the Cunning test. If several laboratories are owned, select the one to use here (best preselected, e.g. the lesser one while travelling). Without a laboratory, brewing is locked (only gathering ingredients and analysing effects).
BREW.DOSES_TOOLTIP: RAW table: own level = elixir level → 1 dose; adept brewing novice → 1d4; master brewing adept → 1d4; master brewing novice → 1d8.
BREW.MATERIALS_TOOLTIP: Half the elixir's list price in shillings (1 alchemy ingredient = 1 shilling of material).
BREW.STOCK_TOOLTIP: Total stock of the resource category „alchemy ingredient“.
BREW.ERR_NO_LEVEL: No active alchemy level — the character cannot brew.
BREW.ERR_NO_LAB: No laboratory in the inventory — brewing is locked (only gathering ingredients and analysing effects).
BREW.ERR_NO_RECIPES: No brewable recipes — missing owned recipes with matching level and tradition access (economy mode).
BREW.ERR_NO_ELIXIRS: No brewable elixirs — no alchemical world items tagged with an alchemy level (RAW mode).
BREW.ERR_NO_MATERIALS: Not enough alchemy ingredients in the inventory (stock: {stock}) — brewing blocked.
BREW.CHAT_MATERIALS_LOST: Ingredients lost: {amount} (raw material of the attempt).
BREW.CHAT_PRODUCED_PARTIAL: Only {count} dose(s) completed — the ingredients were not enough for {planned}.
BREW.CHAT_TERATOS: Teratos potion: {corruption} temporary corruption (1d4 at the end of the brewing test).
REZEPTUR.TARGET_HINT: Drag an elixir item here to link the recipe (sets level, tradition and value).
REZEPTUR.TARGET_TOOLTIP: Drag & drop: alchemical elixir item with a tagged alchemy level.
REZEPTUR.TRADITION_TOOLTIP: Brewing gate: access via an ability/trait/power of the tradition or the boon „Forbidden Knowledge“. Empty = hearsay, freely brewable.
REZEPTUR.PRICE_TOOLTIP: Rules value: 5 × the elixir's list price (base integer in Orteg; set automatically when linking, GM-editable).
REZEPTUR.OWNERSHIP_TOOLTIP: Both values are brewable — bound recipes serve the fief or order.
REZEPTUR.CULTURE_TOOLTIP: Pure flavour — no automation evaluates the culture.
REZEPTUR.ORIGIN_TOOLTIP: Descriptive origin of the recipe (no automation).
REZEPTUR.BASE_TARGET_TOOLTIP: For reverse-engineered or invented recipes: the name of the underlying recipe.
REZEPTUR.INVENTED_TOOLTIP: The recipe was developed or reverse-engineered by the character.
REZEPTUR.ERR_DROP_NOT_ELIXIR: Only alchemical elixir items („is alchemical“ = yes) can be linked.
REZEPTUR.ERR_DROP_NO_LEVEL: The elixir has no alchemy level — tag it on the equipment sheet first.
FACILITY_CATEGORY.LABEL: Laboratory quality
FACILITY_CATEGORY.TOOLTIP: Controls the lab bonus of the brew dialog: simple field laboratory +0, good field laboratory +1, simple stationary laboratory +2, good stationary laboratory +3. Without a laboratory, brewing is locked.
ALCHEMY_MENU.BUTTON_TOOLTIP: Open the alchemy menu (investigate · brew · analyse · reverse-engineer)
BREW.BONUS_NEXT_TOOLTIP: Spends the accumulated reverse-engineering bonus: +1 on this brew.
ANALYSE.GUIDE_TOOLTIP: A guide's higher alchemy level raises the effective level and widens the selection.
ANALYSE.ERR_NO_TARGETS: No analysable elixir within reach (inventory or world, within the effective level).
ANALYSE.CHAT_INGREDIENT: Required ingredient identified: {amount} units per dose
ANALYSE.CHAT_DECEPTION: Deception exposed! The elixir is actually "{name}".
ANALYSE.CHAT_HAS_RECIPE: A recipe for this elixir already exists.
ANALYSE.CHAT_NACHBRAU_HINT: Hint: This elixir can now be reverse-engineered — opening the reverse-engineering dialog.
ANALYSE.WHISPER_DECEPTION: {name} believes they analysed "{false}" — the elixir is actually "{real}".
ANALYSE.WHISPER_NO_DECEPTION: No deception possible: no same-level alternative can be found for "{name}".
ANALYSE.WHISPER_DOSE_LOST: Additionally, one dose of "{name}" was silently destroyed.
ANALYSE.WHISPER_NO_DOSE: The stack of "{name}" is depleted — no further dose damaged.
ANALYSE.TRACE_TOOLTIP: Overrides the automatically derived trace category of the analysis; “automatic” derives the category from the effect fields.
NACHBRAU.BUTTON_TOOLTIP: Reverse-engineer elixir (develop a recipe from dose and base recipe)
NACHBRAU.CHAT_NO_BASE: Re-brewing without base recipe: fixed penalty −10 on the roll
NACHBRAU.ERR_NO_TARGETS: No reverse-engineerable target available (level at most your own, dose available, no duplicates).
NACHBRAU.ERR_NO_ABILITY: This character has no alchemy ability.
NACHBRAU.CHAT_DOSE: One dose of "{name}" was consumed for the analysis.
NACHBRAU.VW_TOOLTIP: Whispers the GM a request for the "Forbidden Knowledge" boon (tradition-gated reverse-engineering).
INVESTIGATE.CHAT_SUCCESS: Something found — the GM decides what the character learns.
INVESTIGATE.WHISPER_BODY: {name} investigates "{subject}" — result: {result}. The revelation is up to you.
UNKNOWN.MARK_TOOLTIP: Applies a cover name and placeholder description — only the GM knows the true identity.
UNKNOWN.MARK_ERR: This elixir is already disguised (misdetermined or marked as unknown).
UNKNOWN.PLACEHOLDER_DESC: The identity of this elixir is unknown — only an analysis can reveal it.
UNKNOWN.BANNER_STACK: one more dose of the stack is silently damaged
SCHEIN.RESET_TOOLTIP: Removes the accumulated reverse-engineering bonus from the character.
SCHEIN.BONUS_BANNER: Reverse-engineering bonus active: +1 on the next brew.
SCHEIN.CHAT_BONUS: Critical success! +1 on the next brew (reverse-engineering bonus).
SCHEIN.CHAT_BOMB: Time bomb! The concoction detonates — {damage} toughness damage.
SCHEIN.WHISPER_BOMB: The recipe "{recipe}" carries a time bomb: the next brew from it detonates automatically.
SCHEIN.EXPOSE_BUTTON_TOOLTIP: Adds the visible fake marker to the recipe name; brewing it still yields only worthless residue.
SCHEIN.ANALYSE_EXPOSED: Fake exposed! The recipe actually describes "{real}" — brewing it would yield only worthless residue.
VW.REQUEST_BODY: {player} requests the "Forbidden Knowledge" boon for {actor} to reverse-engineer "{elixir}" (tradition: {tradition}).
VW.APPLIED_BODY: {actor} receives the "Forbidden Knowledge" boon (tradition: {tradition}, 5 XP cost).
VW.DECLINED_BODY: The request by {actor} for "Forbidden Knowledge" was declined.
RIG.ARMED: Test rig armed: the next roll will be forced to {value}.
RIG.ERR_BAD_VALUE: /rig expects a number from 1 to 20 (e.g. /rig 1 for a critical success, /rig 20 for a fumble).
RIG.CHAT_LINE: Test rig: dice result {value} forced (GM test mode, /rig).
RIG.GM_ONLY: /rig is only available to the GM.
TRAVEL.SETTING_ENABLED_HINT: Enables the travel rules: day-change engine (GM dialog on time jumps, never automatic consumption), travel day dialog with route calculator (table 3.03a), hunger/thirst states and travel status chips. The ration CONSUMPTION additionally runs under its own "Food tracking" and "Water tracking" switches.
TRAVEL.SETTING_FOOD_TRACKING_HINT: Consumes 1 food ration per traveller per travel day from their inventory (half rations: every second day). Off (default) = endless food supplies, no hunger counter.
TRAVEL.SETTING_WATER_TRACKING_HINT: Consumes 1 water ration per traveller per travel day from their inventory. Off (default) = endless water supplies, no thirst counter. Fresh water is usually freely available (02.07) — the switch covers the GM case of scarce water.
TRAVEL.SETTING_NATURAL_HEALING_HINT: Heals every travel group member by 1 Toughness per completed travel day, except on a forced/death march, with hunger, thirst or failed nightmares (card whispered to player and GM). On (default) = automatic healing active.
TRAVEL.SETTING_CORRUPTION_DECAY_HINT: Reduces the temporary corruption of all travel group members outside combat: 1 point per 15 minutes of world time (combat pauses without catch-up). On (default) = decay active.
TRAVEL.MEMBER_ADDED: {name} is now a member of the travel group.
TRAVEL.MEMBER_REMOVED: {name} is no longer a member of the travel group.
TRAVEL.GM_ONLY: Only the GM can manage the travel day.
TRAVEL.FAVOUR_HINT_BOTH: Hunger and thirst: automatic disadvantage (can be overridden)
TRAVEL.STRENGTH_ATTR_DIALOG_HINT: already included in the Strength total
TRAVEL.STRENGTH_AUTOPARAM: Hunger Strength penalty −{penalty} (included in the Strength total)
TRAVEL.STRENGTH_AUTOPARAM_HINT: Persistent penalty from failed hunger tests — already included in the Strength total, not subtracted again.
TRAVEL.CHIP_HUNGER_TOOLTIP: Without food: {food} days · half rations: {ration} days · Strength loss: {loss}
TRAVEL.CHIP_CONSUME_HINT: Click: consume 1 ration for the travel day
TRAVEL.CHIP_SUPPLIED_TOOLTIP: Supplied for the travel day ({count} marker(s)) — completing the travel day consumes the marker instead of booking again
TRAVEL.CONSUME_SELF: Consume — supplied for the travel day
TRAVEL.SELF_NO_STOCK: No stock left in this stack.
TRAVEL.SELF_CONSUMED: {actor} consumed {name} and is supplied for the travel day.
TRAVEL.SUPPLY_SUPPLIED_WARN: {name} is already supplied for the travel day — no further booking needed.
TRAVEL.HUNGER_PROBE_HINT: Daily hunger test against Strength. On a failure the Strength penalty increases by 1 immediately.
TRAVEL.MARCH_PROBE_HINT: Daily exertion test against Strong (death march). On a failure +1d6 damage; on a natural 20 an accident — the GM decides, nothing happens automatically.
TRAVEL.THIRST_PROBE_HINT: Daily thirst test against Strong. On a failure death by dehydration threatens — the GM decides, no automatic death.
TRAVEL.NIGHTMARES_PROBE_HINT: Nightly resolute test against the Nightmares burden. Success: natural healing. Failure: no healing this day.
TRAVEL.NIGHTMARES_CARD_INTRO: {name} battles the nightmares in their sleep!
TRAVEL.NIGHTMARES_REQUEST_MAIN: {name}: Check your nightmares to heal naturally!
TRAVEL.DAY_TOKEN_LOCAL_WARN: {name}: token unlinked — the day booking only applies locally to the token.
TRAVEL.DAY_TOKEN_NONE_WARN: {name}: no linked token — the day booking applies to the world actor (not visible on the token).
TRAVEL.TOKEN_UNLINKED_WARN: Unlinked token: travel state only applies locally here — the travel day books the world actor. Consider linking the token.
TRAVEL.DAY_BREAK_TEXT: World time jumped by {days} travel day(s). Complete the travel day(s) now?
TRAVEL.DAY_BREAK_HINT: Nothing is consumed automatically — the travel-day dialog summarises consumption, counters and consequences.
TRAVEL.MARKER_CELL: Supply markers (advance bookings via chip/context menu) — food: {food}, water: {water}. Completing the travel day consumes one day per marker instead of booking again.
TRAVEL.RATION_HINT: Half rations: only every second day consumes 1 food ration (supplies stretch) — but after 10 days on half rations hunger sets in.
TRAVEL.RATION_OFF_HINT: Ration tracking is off — no rations are consumed and no hunger/thirst counters are kept. Toggle via the GM utility macro.
TRAVEL.WATER_ONLY_HINT: Food tracking is off — only water is consumed.
TRAVEL.PACE_HINT: Forced march: no natural healing. Death march: 1 Toughness per travel day + exertion test (failure +1d6 damage, natural 20 = fatal accident). Loaded characters travel one pace step worse, overloaded characters cannot death march. Camp: no leg and no march consequences — natural healing allowed.
TRAVEL.ADVANCE_OPTION: Advance world time to dawn ({days} day(s))
TRAVEL.ADVANCE_HINT: With Mini Calendar to dawn of the target day, otherwise a core time advance by the calendar's day length.
TRAVEL.SUPPLY_NO_CASTER: No selected travel group member with the Bushcraft boon.
TRAVEL.SUPPLY_SELECT_TEXT: Who searches for supplies? (Only members with the Bushcraft boon.)
TRAVEL.SUPPLY_SELECT_HINT: Players roll themselves via the request card, the GM rolls NPCs directly. Yield: 1d6 on the move, 1d10 focused (total amount).
TRAVEL.FORAGED_TODAY_HINT: Supplies have already been searched for today — a second yield is not possible.
TRAVEL.FORAGED_TODAY_RESULT: Already searched: NO yield (only 1 supply roll per travel day).
TRAVEL.SUPPLY_REQUEST_TEXT: {name} is up: search for supplies via Bushcraft (1d6 on the move / 1d10 focused).
TRAVEL.SUPPLY_REQUEST_HINT: Only sheet owners and the GM can click.
TRAVEL.SUPPLY_ROOM_OVERFLOW: Capacity reached — only {count} room, the rest overflows
TRAVEL.SUPPLY_NO_TARGET: {category}: no refillable ration item found on {name}
TRAVEL.BOOKING_TEXT: {name} found {count} ration(s) — choose targets and amounts:
TRAVEL.BOOKING_LOAD_HINT: Preview: if the booking worsens the load state, the line turns red.
TRAVEL.BOOKING_CARD_GIVE_HINT: Give buttons (GM only) open the give dialog.
TRAVEL.TRACKING_ON_CHAT: Ration tracking ON — 1 food ration and 1 water ration are consumed per travel day.
TRAVEL.MASTER_ON_NOTE: Travel rules (master switch) activated as well.
TRAVEL.CARD_ENDURING_GROUP: Enduring March: The travel group gains a second chance on the exertion test.
TRAVEL.CARD_ENDURING_HEAL: Enduring March: heals during forced/death march
TRAVEL.CARD_FOOTNOTE: Tests open the roll dialog (disadvantage preselected, but overridable). The GM applies consequences via the buttons — nothing happens automatically.
TRAVEL.CARD_DEATH_HUNGER: {name} reaches Strength 0 — death by starvation is at the GM's discretion.
TRAVEL.CARD_DEATH_THIRST: {name} fails the daily thirst test — death by dehydration is at the GM's discretion.
TRAVEL.CARD_ACCIDENT: {name} suffers a fatal accident (natural 20) — how to proceed is up to the GM.
TRAVEL.APPLY_STRENGTH_LOSS: Strength loss of {name} increased by 1 (hunger test failed).
TRAVEL.TAGGING_HEADER: Suggestions via name heuristics — selectable per row. Already tagged items no longer appear.
TRAVEL.TAGGING_HINT: Covers world items and all inventories; compendiums remain untouched. Repeatable.
TRAVEL.TAGGING_NONE_FOUND: No untagged candidates for food/water rations found.
TRAVEL.CAPMIG_HEADER: Convert ration capacity items (food/water ration category with capacity > 0) to the new model: item quantity → 1, ration fill level → “Ration count”. Prefilled with min(quantity, capacity), editable per row.
TRAVEL.CAPMIG_HINT: Covers world items and all inventories; already migrated items no longer appear. Repeatable.
TRAVEL.CAPMIG_DONE: {count} capacity items migrated (quantity 1, ration fill level set).
TRAVEL.CAPMIG_NONE_FOUND: No migratable capacity rations found (without an already set ration fill level).
AOE.SETTING_ENABLED_HINT: Unlocks the tier-1 area automation: GM-only "Zone" tab on mystical power sheets, interactive template placement (1 square = 2 meters combat scale, regardless of scene calibration) and automatic target proposal for the tokens inside the area. Default: enabled.
AOE.INFO_SCALE: Tier 1 works purely in squares: 1 square = 2 meters (combat scale), regardless of scene calibration. The target filter compares token disposition against the caster.
AOE.INFO_SIZE: Radius for circle and cone, length for line (width 1 square), side length for rectangle — each in squares.
AOE.INFO_TARGETING: Determines which tokens inside the area are marked as targets automatically: all of them, or the enemy or ally side via disposition comparison against the caster.
AOE.INFO_DEFAULTS: RAW recommendation for the five tier-1 powers (Draining Glyph, Blinding Symbol, Battle Symbol, Banishing Seal, Holy Aura): circle, radius 5 squares — RAW anchor "short distance" = 10 meters.
AOE.ERR_DISABLED: Area Effects (AoE) are disabled in the world settings.
AOE.ERR_NO_SCENE: No active scene — the zone can only be placed on a battlemap.
AOE.ERR_NO_CONFIG: No area configured — pick a shape in the zone tab.
AOE.CHAT_NO_TARGETS: No visible token inside the area.
AOE.CHAT_TARGETED: The tokens inside are marked as targets.
AOE.ERR_NO_POWER_AUTOMATION: This power has no scripted automation – zone effect unavailable.
AOE.ERR_SOURCE_GONE: Source power or actor is no longer available.
AOE.FREE_HINT: Empty fields = no effect. Formulas use Foundry dice notation (e.g. 1d6).
AOE.INFO_DURATION: Duration in rounds; 0 = unlimited (runs until the end button). Out of combat, 15 minutes of world time count as one round.
AOE.INFO_MODE: Instant: effect once on placement. Lasting: zone persists (trigger button/on enter).
AOE.INFO_TRIGGER: On enter: triggers automatically when a token enters. Manual: only via the trigger button.
AOE.SETTING_PLAYERS_HINT: Players who own the item may place areas from their own mystical powers (zone tab).
AOE.ONESHOT_HINT: One-time effect: mark targets yourself if needed (the first marked target is the primary target), then trigger. The zone disappears afterwards.
AOE.INFO_TARGET_ORDER: Determines which tokens in the zone are captured: With marking order, the triggerer's own target markers override the filter (the first marked target is the primary target); nearest to center sorts by distance to the zone center; scene order keeps the scene's order.
AOE.EXEC_HINT: How should the power be executed?
